data.name: Launcher.Help.Automation
data.value: Help: how do my players join?

data.name: Launcher.Status.Starting
data.value: Lighting the candles… (the first start takes a little longer)

data.name: Launcher.Lan.Toggle
data.value: Let players on my network join

data.name: Launcher.Lan.Hint
data.value: Your firewall may ask the first time: allow private networks. Players on other networks need a VPN or tunnel, such as Tailscale.

data.name: Launcher.Welcome.Intro
data.value: Characters, rules, your world and a live table, all running on this computer. Who will be playing?

data.name: Launcher.Welcome.HostBody
data.value: Players join from their phones or laptops on your Wi-Fi. I'll show you a code to scan.

data.name: Launcher.Welcome.SoloBody
data.value: Only this computer can open it. You can open it to players later.

data.name: Launcher.Welcome.Footer
data.value: You can change this any time in the launcher. The ? button explains how players join.

data.name: Launcher.Check.SummaryProblems
data.value: Found something to fix. Start at the first red item.

data.name: Launcher.Check.SummaryWarnings
data.value: Nothing is broken, but check the yellow items.

data.name: Launcher.Check.SummaryOk
data.value: Everything I can check looks fine. If a player still cannot connect, see the last item.

data.name: Launcher.Qr.Instruction
data.value: Point your phone's camera at this. It opens the table in the browser.

data.name: Launcher.Qr.SameWifi
data.value: Phones must be on the same Wi-Fi as this computer.

data.name: Launcher.Help.Intro
data.value: TTRPG.Codex runs on this computer. Your players open it in their web browser: nothing to install for them.

data.name: Launcher.Help.Head.Room
data.value: Playing in the same room or on the same Wi-Fi

data.name: Launcher.Help.Room2
data.value: Click {0} next to “{1}” and let them scan it with their phone camera. Or click {2} and send it to them.

data.name: Launcher.Help.Room3
data.value: They open the link in a browser on their phone, tablet or laptop. It must be on the same Wi-Fi as you.

data.name: Launcher.Help.Room4
data.value: In your campaign, copy the invite link from the Overview page and send it too. They make an account and they are in.

data.name: Launcher.Help.AwayIntro
data.value: Your computer is not on the internet, so players elsewhere need a private link to it. The easiest free way is Tailscale (tailscale.com):

data.name: Launcher.Help.Away1
data.value: You and each player install Tailscale and sign in (a few minutes, free for small groups).

data.name: Launcher.Help.Away2
data.value: In Tailscale, share this computer with each player.

data.name: Launcher.Help.Away3
data.value: Turn on “{0}”. A “{1}” link appears: copy it and send it to them. They open it in their browser while Tailscale is on.

data.name: Launcher.Help.Trouble1
data.value: Your computer asked about the network or firewall? Allow it for private or home networks.

data.name: Launcher.Help.Trouble2
data.value: Guest or café Wi-Fi often stops devices from seeing each other. Use your normal Wi-Fi, or Tailscale.

data.name: Launcher.Help.Trouble3
data.value: Click “{0}” in the launcher: it checks the server, the network and the address, and tells you what to fix.

data.name: Launcher.Help.Trouble4
data.value: Your computer's address can change when you restart it or join another network. If so, copy the new link from the launcher and send it again.

data.name: Launcher.Help.Trouble5
data.value: Keep this computer awake and plugged in while you play. If it sleeps, players are disconnected.

data.name: Launcher.Help.Good1
data.value: Closing this window does not stop the game. It keeps running from the tray icon (menu bar on a Mac). Use {0} to stop it for good.

data.name: Launcher.Help.Good2
data.value: Your campaigns are saved on this computer ({0}), with a daily backup ({1}).

data.name: Launcher.Help.Good3
data.value: Only people with your link can reach it, and only while the launcher is running.

data.name: Launcher.Help.Good4
data.value: Something wrong? Open the {0} and send it to whoever is helping you.

data.name: Launcher.Join.Running.Detail
data.value: It is up on this computer at {0}.

data.name: Launcher.Join.Starting.Detail
data.value: Give it a minute (the first start is slower), then check again.

data.name: Launcher.Join.PortBusy.Detail
data.value: Close the other program (it may be another copy of TTRPG.Codex), then press {0}.

data.name: Launcher.Join.LanOn.Detail
data.value: Players on your Wi-Fi are allowed in.

data.name: Launcher.Join.LanOff.Detail
data.value: Only this computer can open the table. Turn on “{0}”.

data.name: Launcher.Join.NoAddress.Title
data.value: This computer has no network address

data.name: Launcher.Join.NoAddress.Detail
data.value: It does not look connected to Wi-Fi or a cable. Connect to your network, then check again.

data.name: Launcher.Join.Odd.Title
data.value: That address does not look like a home network

data.name: Launcher.Join.Odd.Detail
data.value: Home and office networks usually start with 192.168 or 10. A VPN may be on, or you may be on a public network. Players on your Wi-Fi may need to use a different address.

data.name: Launcher.Join.Multi.Title
data.value: This computer has more than one address

data.name: Launcher.Join.Multi.Detail
data.value: If the first link does not work, try one of these: {0}.

data.name: Launcher.Join.Answers.Title
data.value: The server answers on your network address

data.name: Launcher.Join.Answers.Detail
data.value: This computer can reach itself at that link.

data.name: Launcher.Join.NoAnswer.Title
data.value: The server does not answer on your network address

data.name: Launcher.Join.NoAnswer.Detail
data.value: Network access may have been switched on after the server started: press {0}, then {1}.

data.name: Launcher.Join.Tailscale.Detail
data.value: Friends who are not on your Wi-Fi can use {0} if they have Tailscale and you have shared this computer with them.

data.name: Launcher.Join.Unknown.Title
data.value: What I cannot check from here

data.name: Launcher.Join.Unknown.Detail
data.value: Your firewall and your Wi-Fi router. If everything above is fine and a player still cannot connect: allow TTRPG.Codex through the firewall for private networks when your computer asks, make sure their phone is on the same Wi-Fi (not mobile data), and avoid guest Wi-Fi, which often blocks devices from seeing each other.

data.name: Launcher.Server.StartFailed
data.value: The server could not be started: {0}

data.name: Launcher.Server.NoAnswer
data.value: The server did not answer in time. See the log for details.

data.name: Launcher.Server.Unexpected
data.value: The server stopped unexpectedly. Another program may be using the port. See the log for details.
